result_text:
Template literals now get the same treatment as `"..."` and `'...'` literals when units are compared for duplication. I didn't add a test or run an end-to-end check on your `alpha`/`beta` example. The existing `codeanalyzer` tests I ran (`*JavaScript*`, `*CStyle*`, `*Cpp*`, `*Unit*`) pass.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`. It replaces `` `...` `` with ` `` `, right after the single-quote line. The JavaScript extractor inherits from this class, so it picks it up. Code outside the literals is untouched, so a difference there still keeps units apart.

Like the existing `"..."` and `'...'` rules, this only matches a template literal that sits on one line. A literal that spans several lines isn't normalized. I left that alone because collapsing newlines would shift the line mapping used for unit boundaries.
